fieldNotes.siteResolution: Supplied approx coords (32.5690,-95.2150) and the street-number geocode of '3265 (S) FM 2869' both landed in empty East Texas timberland ~10-20 km off (rural FM road number interpolation is unreliable here). Resolved the plant by geocoding the NAMED place 'Ozarka Plant, Hawkins TX' -> 32.6668,-95.1925, which lands directly on a single very large light-blue-roofed industrial building set in cleared timberland NE of Hawkins. Confirmed by web research: the Ozarka / Primo Brands (BlueTriton) Wood County bottling plant is a ~618,000 sq ft facility at 3265 S FM 2869, rebuilt and reopened after a 2023 tornado. Building footprint, water-treatment ponds at two corners, process tanks/silos, and the spring-water context all match. Locked center 32.66655,-95.19120.
fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm, sliding/swing gate, or guard booth is visible at any pinch point. The single internal paved drive runs NW from the building/parking area to an unpaved perimeter ring road (z19/z20 north-junction crops show only a dirt road crossing and electrical/transmission pylons, no booth or arm). The property is gated only by remoteness (deep private timberland, ~1.5 km off the nearest public road). Marked false. Low confidence: a manned or arm gate could sit further out along the private approach beyond the captured frames, and there is zero Street View coverage anywhere within ~1.5 km to verify.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No booth-sized structure (1-3 vehicle footprint, multi-side windows) at the entrance drive or perimeter-road junction. False.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because no truck gate is confirmed; if controlled access exists it is unverified.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Continuous dock bank along the building's long SW-facing wall plus a second bank on the SE/E face by the process tanks and a covered dock canopy (z18/z19 SW-wall + west-office crops). Trailers backed in along both faces in a regular rhythm. Honest estimate ~50-60 total doors across the ~300 m+ SW wall and the SE bank -> banded 50+. The exact count is hard to read where trailers occlude doors, so dockDoorCount=55 is approximate (flagged).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Massive dedicated trailer drop yard fills the SW quadrant: many long marked rows of trailers parked without tractors (z20 dropyard + dockbank2 crops show 8-10 rows of stalls). Easily 50+ -> banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropYard: True - the SW lot is a distinct, dedicated trailer-storage area separate from the active dock aprons that wrap the building.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Two physically distinct dock clusters on different building faces (long SW wall bank + SE/E-face bank near the process tanks) suggest split ship/receive, but function cannot be confirmed from imagery -> medium confidence.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved internal apron wraps the S and E of the building between the dock banks and the drop yard, acting as an internal queue/staging area; traced as 'staging'.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long private internal approach (NW drive ~0.4 km from the perimeter road to the building) plus a deep internal apron -> easily holds a 3+ truck queue before the docks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide, lightly-used paved aprons and a single open entrance with abundant unused width -> ample room to add a bypass/express lane. True.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Single shared internal access drive; lane striping not resolvable. Estimated 1 in / 1 out, flagged.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: One internal drive serves both directions to/from the perimeter road -> entry/exit together.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~80-100 in the SW drop-yard rows + ~20-30 backed at the SW/SE dock banks + a few staged on the apron = ~120, approximate across overlapping imagery vintages.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: The drop yard's 8-10 marked rows hold ~120-140 trailers at capacity; adding apron and dock positions pushes practical capacity to ~160.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~60.5 acres of cleared/paved/built footprint inside the perimeter ring road derived from the perimeter polygon; the surrounding company-owned spring/timber land is far larger but is forest, not yard.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property; access is by the private road only. False.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale / weigh pad visible in the truck path. False.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Site is isolated in East Texas timberland with no adjacent development and the nearest town (Hawkins) several km away -> likely weaker cellular coverage. Inferred, medium confidence.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: One dominant manufacturing/DC building plus an attached/adjacent office annex at the W corner counted as the complex -> 2; process tanks/silos and water-treatment ponds are ancillary, not counted as buildings.
fieldNotes.imageryQuality: Maxar/Airbus tiles are sharp and recent enough to read dock rhythm, trailer rows, ponds, and tanks clearly. The only gap is ground-level verification of the gate (no Street View within ~1.5 km).
